title: Avoid plain cross-fades as the only transition
body: Cross-fades between every scene look amateur and slow. Prefer cuts, matched motion, wipes or zooms that fit the style.

title: Do not animate everything at once
body: Simultaneous unrelated motions compete. Stagger, prioritise, and let some elements rest.

title: Music must not fight the voice
body: Duck music under speech; avoid vocals in background music under narration.

title: Text on a plain background is not a video
body: A scene with only words on a background is rejected. Every sentence needs a visual that shows it (scene piece, UI, chart, footage, object).

title: Avoid tiny text on mobile
body: Nothing under ~32 px at 1080 width. If it does not fit, cut words or split the scene.

title: One master, many formats
body: Design for the tallest format first, keep key content in the centre-safe area, then make 1:1 and 16:9 versions by re-framing, not squashing.

title: B-roll on every claim
body: When the speaker mentions something visual (a product, a place, a number), cut to it. 2–4 s per b-roll shot; return to the speaker for emotion and the close.

title: Captions that people read
body: 2–5 words per line, max 2 lines, high contrast with outline or box, highlight the keyword, sync to speech within 100 ms, keep clear of platform UI (bottom 15–20%). Most social views are muted.

title: Colour: correct, then grade
body: First balance exposure and white balance so skin looks natural and shots match; then apply one consistent look. Keep skin tones on the skin-tone line.

title: Cut on action
body: Cut in the middle of a movement (a turn, a hand reaching); the motion carries the eye across the cut and hides it.

title: End on the call to action
body: Finish with one clear action (follow, download, visit) held at least 1.5 s with the brand. Do not fade to black early or end on a weak sentence.

title: Reframing to vertical
body: Track the face and keep eyes near the upper third; leave headroom for captions and hook text; avoid cutting off hands during gestures.

title: Hook in the first 1–3 seconds
body: Open with the most interesting moment, a bold claim, a question or a visual surprise. No logos, greetings or slow fades first. On social, 50–70% of viewers decide in 2 s.

title: Loudness targets
body: Social and YouTube: integrated −14 LUFS, true peak −1 dBTP. Voice is the priority; music −18 to −22 dB under speech (ducking), back up in gaps.

title: Lower thirds and labels
body: Name and title appear for 3–4 s on first appearance, animate in/out, sit in the lower third clear of captions, in brand style.

title: Montage
body: A fast sequence of related shots over music shows time passing or variety. Vary angles and sizes; build speed towards the end.

title: Cut to the music
body: Detect beats (media beats) and land cuts and big motions on beats or bar starts; hold quiet moments on phrases; end on the final hit, never mid-phrase.

title: Pattern interrupts
body: Every 3–6 s change something: angle, zoom, graphic, b-roll, sound effect, colour. Monotony is the main cause of drop-off.

title: Punch-ins hide jump cuts
body: Alternate framing 100% / 115–130% between consecutive jump cuts so they feel deliberate. Punch in on emphasis words.

title: Remove dead air and fillers
body: Cut pauses over ~0.5 s and filler words (um, uh, like, you know) in talking heads; keep breaths that sound natural. Hide jump cuts with punch-ins or b-roll.

title: Sound design on visual events
body: Every pop, swipe and click deserves a short sound (whoosh, pop, click, riser into reveals) at low volume. Sound makes motion feel twice as smooth.

title: Speed ramps
body: Ramp from normal to fast into a transition and slow back out, or slow down on the key moment. Keep ramps on beats for impact.

title: Stabilise shaky footage
body: Stabilise handheld shots with a small crop (5–8%); do not stabilise intentional camera moves. Re-check edges for warping.

title: Right-to-left motion for Kurdish and Arabic
body: For Sorani, Arabic and Persian: text reads right to left, so wipes, slides and lists enter from the right; progress fills right to left; never split or reverse shaped letters; use the existing Kurdish fonts only.

title: Sorani captions
body: Break lines at phrase boundaries, 2–4 words per line, a little more line height than Latin (1.4–1.6), keep numbers and Latin brand names in their own direction runs.

title: 3D hero objects
body: Render 3D products or icons with soft studio light and a slow turntable or 10–20° rotation; one hero per scene, ground shadow for weight; match the palette to the brand.

title: Anticipation before a big move
body: A tiny opposite move (2–6%) or a 60–120 ms hold before a large motion tells the viewer something is about to happen. Use before reveals, launches and swaps.

title: Move along arcs, not straight lines
body: Objects travelling far (cards flying to avatars, icons to a cart) look natural on a slight arc. Combine with scale-down as they reach the target.

title: Colour roles: 60-30-10
body: 60% background/neutral, 30% brand primary, 10% accent for the things to notice (buttons, highlights, key numbers). An accent everywhere is no accent.

title: Carry motion across cuts
body: The direction and speed of the exit should feed the next entrance (exit left → enter from right; zoom in → next scene starts large). Matched motion hides the cut.

title: Contrast and readability
body: Text on background at least 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for very large display type). Never put text on busy footage without a scrim, shadow or solid shape behind it.

title: Cursor demonstrates the product
body: A cursor gliding on an eased arc to a button, a press, a ripple and an immediate UI response shows "how easy" better than any sentence. Keep it 1–2 clicks per scene.

title: Depth with shadow, blur and parallax
body: Front layers move faster than back layers (parallax 1.0 / 0.6 / 0.3). Bigger shadow and slight scale-up for elements coming forward; background blur to separate focus.

title: Durations by size and distance
body: Small UI elements 150–300 ms; cards and panels 300–500 ms; full-screen moves and scene transitions 500–800 ms. Larger distance = slightly longer. In a 30 s social video, nothing important animates slower than 0.8 s.

title: Never move things linearly
body: Real objects accelerate and decelerate. Use ease-out (cubic/quint) for entrances, ease-in for exits, ease-in-out for moves on screen. Linear only for constant loops (rotation, scrolling tickers, progress fills).

title: Plan the eye path
body: Place the next thing to look at where the eye already is, or lead it there with motion. Vertical video: top third for the message, centre for the visual, bottom kept clear for captions and UI.

title: Follow-through and overlapping action
body: Parts do not stop at the same time: a card lands, its shadow and content settle 60–150 ms later. Secondary elements trail the primary one.

title: Use a grid and consistent margins
body: Align everything to a 4 or 8 px grid, keep the same outer margins in every scene, and repeat positions for repeating elements so the video feels designed, not assembled.

title: Holds stay alive
body: After elements land, keep a subtle life: 1–3% push-in, slow drift, parallax, a blinking cursor, a counter ticking. A frozen frame longer than ~1.5 s reads as a mistake.

title: Animated icons
body: Icons should draw on (stroke) or pop with overshoot, not fade. Keep one icon family per video (same stroke width and corner style).

title: Kinetic typography rules
body: Animate by word or phrase, never letter-by-letter for long lines (unreadable). Keep each phrase on screen at least 0.3 s per word. Emphasise one keyword per line with colour, scale (1.15–1.3×) or a highlight sweep.

title: Seamless loops
body: For looping backgrounds and GIF-like pieces, make the last frame match the first (same position, phase); use sine motion or full rotations so there is no jump.

title: Reveal with masks
body: Text and shapes rising from behind an invisible line (overflow clip) look more designed than fades. Wipe direction follows reading direction (right-to-left for Kurdish and Arabic).

title: Count numbers up, never just show them
body: Animate numbers from 0 (or the old value) with ease-out over 0.8–1.4 s, tabular figures so width stays stable, and a small pulse or colour flash when they land.

title: One main motion at a time
body: At any moment the eye should have one primary moving thing. Secondary motion is smaller, slower or lower contrast. Two competing big moves read as noise.

title: Overshoot and settle for life
body: A 5–12% overshoot (back or spring easing) makes pops feel physical. Use it on icons, badges, buttons and counters; not on large text blocks or backgrounds.

title: Subtle squash for UI presses
body: A button press: scale 0.94–0.96 for 80–120 ms then back with a slight overshoot, plus a ripple or colour change. Cursor clicks should always show this feedback.

title: Stagger related elements 40–80 ms
body: Lists, words, tiles and icons enter one after another, 40–80 ms apart (up to 120 ms for big cards). Same direction and easing for the group; the eye reads the order as hierarchy.

title: Type scale for vertical video
body: At 1080×1920: headline 90–140 px, supporting 48–64 px, labels 32–40 px. 2–5 words per line, at most 3 lines on screen. Keep text inside 150 px top and 300 px bottom safe zones (platform UI).

title: A visual event every 1–2 s
body: Short-form social: a new visual event (element enters, number changes, cut, highlight) every 1–2 s; scenes of 2–5 s. Long-form explainers can breathe to 3–4 s between events.

title: 6-second bumper ad
body: One idea: brand or product in the first second, one benefit, one visual, logo and CTA in the last 1.5 s.

title: LinkedIn video basics
body: 1:1 or 4:5 performs well, autoplay muted so captions are required, 30–90 s, professional tone, data and outcomes up front.

title: TikTok, Reels, Shorts basics
body: 1080×1920, 30 fps. Hook in 1–2 s, 15–45 s performs well for promos, captions on, keep the bottom 20% and right edge clear of UI, loop-friendly endings.

title: YouTube long-form basics
body: 16:9, 1920×1080 or 4K, chapters, a 5–15 s cold open hook, visual change every 3–5 s, end screen space for the last 5–20 s.

title: App launch
body: Phone mockup hero, tilted reveal, swipe through 3 key screens with cursor/tap feedback, store badges and CTA. Music with a build and a drop on the reveal.

title: Event recap
body: Music-driven montage: arrival, crowd, speakers, details, emotion shots, best quote, logo. Cut on beats, speed ramps into drops, 30–60 s.

title: Explainer
body: Problem → why it matters → how it works (3 steps, one visual metaphor each) → benefit → CTA. Steady pacing, one idea per scene, icons and diagrams over text.

title: Product ad
body: Product hero in motion in the first second, 3 benefits as quick visual proofs, price/offer, CTA. Close-ups, hand interactions, satisfying motions.

title: SaaS promo (30 s)
body: Hook with the pain (notifications piling up) → product reveal in a browser or phone mockup → 3 features as demos (cursor clicks, cards moving, dashboard counting) → proof (number counter, logos, quote) → CTA with logo. 6–8 scenes of 3–5 s.

title: Talking-head short
body: Tighten (remove pauses and fillers), hook text for 2 s, punch-ins every 2–3 cuts, b-roll on claims, word captions with keyword colour, SFX on graphics, CTA end card.

title: Customer testimonial
body: Strongest quote as the hook, name lower third, problem → result in their words, b-roll of the product in use, result number on screen, logo at the end.

title: Tutorial / how-to
body: State the result first, then numbered steps with screen recording or UI mockups, zoom on the click area, cursor highlights, recap at the end.

title: Premium product reveal
body: Dark or pure white backgrounds, slow camera moves, dramatic light on the product, minimal large type, long eases (0.8–1.5 s), lots of negative space, music builds. Launches, hardware, luxury.

title: Clay / soft 3D
body: Rounded soft 3D objects with matte materials, pastel palette, gentle bounces and squash. Friendly explainers, education, consumer apps.

title: Paper collage / cut-out
body: Cut-out photos with white borders and shadows, torn paper, stop-motion feel (12 fps steps), mixed textures. Editorial, culture, social campaigns.

title: Data visualisation explainer
body: Charts that build, numbers that count, maps that light up, clear labels and sources. News, finance, reports. Accuracy first; every number sourced.

title: Documentary
body: Interviews with b-roll, slow pacing, lower thirds, archival footage, music under emotional beats, natural sound. Trust, brand stories, case studies.

title: Hand-drawn / doodle
body: Sketchy strokes that draw on, boil animation (redrawn lines 8–12 fps), paper textures. Education, storytelling, warm brands.

title: Flat 2D explainer
body: Flat vector characters and objects, limited palette, shape-based motion, icons that pop. Classic explainers; cheap to make consistent.

title: Glassmorphism
body: Frosted translucent panels (background blur, 1 px light border), colourful blurred gradients behind, floating depth. Fintech, apps, modern tech. Keep contrast on text.

title: Glitch / digital
body: RGB split, scanlines, data-mosh cuts, flicker on the beat. Gaming, cyber, tech launches. Use in short bursts; long glitch is tiring.

title: Isometric illustration
body: 30° isometric scenes (buildings, devices, data centres) with small moving parts and paths. Systems, logistics, how-it-works explainers.

title: Bold kinetic typography
body: Huge words filling the frame, fast swaps on the beat, high contrast (black/white + one accent), scale and position jumps. Hooks, quotes, motivational, music-driven.

title: Liquid / organic shapes
body: Morphing blobs and gradients, smooth sine motion, circular transitions. Wellness, beauty, music.

title: Minimal monochrome
body: One or two colours, lots of space, thin type, slow precise moves. Architecture, fashion, premium services.

title: Neo-brutalism
body: Thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, saturated flat colours, chunky type, snappy linear-ish moves and stamps. Young brands, creators, playful tech.

title: Podcast / talking clip
body: Vertical crop on the speaker, word-by-word bold captions with keyword colour, punch-ins on emphasis, progress bar, hook text at top for the first 2 s.

title: Retro / Y2K
body: Chrome type, gradients, pixel or VHS textures, starbursts, bouncy loops. Music, fashion, nostalgia campaigns.

title: Clean SaaS / product UI
body: Light background, soft shadows, rounded cards (12–24 px), UI mockups in phone/browser frames, cursor demos, counters and charts, smooth ease-out moves. Software, startups, apps.

title: Swiss / International typographic
body: Strict grid, bold sans-serif (Helvetica/Inter style), big type as the main visual, flat colour blocks, red/black/white or brand colours, sharp cuts and slides on the grid. Corporate, editorial, informative.

title: Cinematic trailer
body: Building rhythm: slow open, rising cuts on percussion, title cards between beats, a drop, a final hit and logo. Launches, events, films.

title: UGC / native social
body: Phone-shot talking head, quick jump cuts, on-screen captions in platform style, text hooks, zoom punch-ins, green-screen backgrounds. Ads that should not look like ads.

title: YouTube retention editing
body: Hook in the first 5 s, constant visual change every 2–4 s (cuts, zooms, b-roll, graphics, memes), sound effects on every pop, captions for key words, no dead air.

title: The cut is the default transition
body: Most changes should be cuts on action or on the beat. Use designed transitions to signal a change of idea, not between every shot.

title: J-cuts and L-cuts
body: Let audio lead (J-cut: hear the next scene before seeing it) or trail (L-cut: keep the voice while cutting to b-roll). Makes dialogue edits smooth and natural.

title: Match cut
body: Cut between two shots with matching shape, motion or position (circle → coin → planet; hand swipe → page swipe). Feels clever and keeps flow.

title: Morph between states
body: The same element changes shape/size/position into the next layout (card → full screen, button → page). Strongest for product storytelling.

title: Shape and colour wipes
body: A brand-coloured shape sweeps across, covering the old scene and uncovering the new. Keep direction consistent through the video; 0.4–0.6 s.

title: Whip pan / motion blur transition
body: Fast directional move with motion blur over 6–10 frames out of one scene and into the next in the same direction. Great for energy and travel.

title: Zoom-through
body: Scale into an element (a screen, a letter, a hole) until it fills the frame and becomes the next scene. Add 4–10 px blur at peak speed.
